en: Now, this current solution has a problem.
As you saw before, clicking the back button
doesn't work because even though we navigate
to a different page, or at least it looks
like we do that,
you also see if you take a look at the URL
here that this never changes. The URL stays
the same.
So to the browser, we never left the old
page and that's why the back button doesn't
work.
Of course, typically you would want it to
work even if you are building a single page
application because the user Users of the
website should still have that feeling of
navigating between different pages.
You just technically never left that one
page,
but it still should give users all the
features they would expect from a multi-page
application, like being able to use the
forward and backward buttons.
And that's why you can add another attribute
here to this anchor element.
And that's the hx-push-url
attribute.
This attribute here can be used to update
the browser URL and also to save the
previous page snapshot so that users can use
the back button and HTMX will do all the
heavy lifting behind the scenes.
So here we could then navigate to /products/
and then maybe inject that product ID
so that the URL that will be displayed in
the browser bar will be this URL or will
include this path here and we'll be able to
use the back button.
So with this attribute added, if we now save
that
and we reload this page, if I click on a
product, you now see the URL was updated. It
now includes these details here.
And I can now use the back button and then
also the forward button to go back to the
page I was before.
So that now works and that's now a much
better single page application feeling.
And we could now do that on all our anchor
elements to make sure that we actually use
HTMX for loading the next page's content and
for replacing the current page content with
that.
But as it turns out, there is an even better
way of doing that.
